title: The Climate Investment Trust
subtitle: Hold capital, lend its strength
message: Donors will not vote for large cash transfers. A trust that holds capital instead of spending it can take second loss behind policy guarantees. On the development banks' loss record each donor dollar delivers about 80 dollars of interest savings rather than one; in a stress case without their preferred-creditor status, 2.7.

problem.text: Grants buy one project and are gone. Payments against counterfactual baselines reward delay. And sovereigns do not pay their peers, so an international feebate needs a trust to hold the pot.

mechanism.title: One pool, three jobs
mechanism.caption: A: interest savings per donor dollar, stress, middle and base (MDB record) cases. B: Trust capital over 25 years from $5bn at launch, base case.
points: Second loss: the government first, the Trust second, a AAA entity last. A 0.5% buffer keeps exhaustion to 1% a year on the MDB record; 9.3% in the stress case.
Investment: co-invest for 25% of private returns; regional funds hold first-loss tranches (Brief 2.2).
Accounts: credited by performance, pledgeable as collateral now, drawn after 2050.

action.title: Launch it as insurance first
results: $5bn ($1bn grants, $4bn country stakes): up to ~$1tn of guarantees on the MDB record; $54bn in the stress case, saving borrowers $1.6bn a year.
Insurance only, it must charge about 0.02% a year on exposure to hold steady (0.8% in the stress case).
$95bn of co-investment yields $2.4bn a year in fees: $23bn after 10 years, about $57bn in the long run ($28bn in the stress case).
